name: Maffucci Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical diagnosis based on characteristic features

criteria.description: Presence of multiple enchondromas (benign cartilaginous bone tumors)
Presence of multiple soft tissue hemangiomas (vascular malformations)
Evidence of malignant transformation of enchondromas or hemangiomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple enchondromas and multiple soft tissue hemangiomas
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and radiological; genetic testing for IDH1/IDH2 mutations may support diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Typically affects long bones and phalanges
Includes limb length discrepancy and bone deformities

common.notes: Often related to enchondroma growth or fractures

occasional.notes: Due to bone deformities or hemangiomas near joints
Small dilated blood vessels on skin surface

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression
rare.notes: From large hemangiomas or bone lesions
Chronic blood loss from vascular lesions
Due to lymphatic obstruction by hemangiomas

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests unless bleeding or anemia present
imaging: Radiographs showing multiple enchondromas with characteristic radiolucent lesions and endosteal scalloping
MRI demonstrating soft tissue hemangiomas and extent of bone lesions
Bone scans may show increased uptake in affected areas
genetic: Somatic mosaic mutations in IDH1 and IDH2 genes detected in affected tissues

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of multiple enchondromas without soft tissue hemangiomas
Primarily vascular lesions without skeletal involvement

redFlags: Rapid increase in size of enchondromas or hemangiomas
New onset of severe bone pain
Signs of malignant transformation such as swelling, ulceration, or neurological deficits
references: Maffucci E. Di una forma particolare di osteodistrofia: con note critiche e bibliografiche. G Chir. 1881;2:423-429.
Pansuriya TC, et al. Somatic mosaic IDH1 and IDH2 mutations are associated with enchondroma and spindle cell hemangioma in Ollier disease and Maffucci syndrome. Nat Genet. 2011;43(12):1256-1261.
